## {.vcenter .lattice}

::: {.card style="text-align:center; max-width:640px; margin:0 auto;"}
[SAY ≠ DO]{style="font-family:'Bebas Neue',sans-serif; font-size:2em; letter-spacing:0.03em; color:var(--accent);"}

::: {.notes}
- [SLOW] Poll result ≠ the point. Asked to SHOW what a questionnaire gives: SAY, not DO
- [VERBATIM] "Surveys tell you what people SAY they'd do. An exercise shows you what they DO. That's what this hour is about."
- Observable: DO is timeable. First strange call → someone with a mandate on the line, in minutes
- Contract: play 1 round · vote a real decision · free guide for next week
- [CALLBACK] same words close the hour after Q&A
:::

## An exercise can also end up as SAY. {.vcenter}

::: {.card style="text-align:center; max-width:640px; margin:0 auto;"}
Not WHETHER you practice. HOW.
:::

{{< include illus/bubbles.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- Not WHETHER, but does it change what people DO
- "Tabletop" covers everything: slideshow read aloud, signature at the end = SAY with extra steps
- Same label, opposite exercise: one where people argue, decide, get it wrong, feel it
- Difference is not the format name, it is whether anyone had to DECIDE under pressure
- Phishing tests: click rate is a dial, measures the tester
- Gotcha tests cost trust; one click is enough
- Butcher: interesting part starts AFTER the click
- [~35s] master frame for next 10 min
:::

## IT is not a cost. IT is a precondition. {.vcenter}

{{< include illus/foundation.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- [FRAME] Why this matters here: the exercise budget comes from how leadership sees IT
- Orgs don't see themselves as IT companies; a municipality IS one, every service runs on it
- IT = cost to keep down → security = lowest passable level
- [BEAT] "…right up until the first ransomware attack."
- → cost mindset is WHY exercises become a minimum compliance tick instead of training
- [~45s]
:::

## NIS2 · ISO 27001: Practice is MANDATORY. The format isn't. {.vcenter}

::: {.feature-grid style="--fg-cols:4;"}
- People don't open up
- Egos clash
- "It can't happen here"
- Fun is taboo
:::

{{< include illus/stamp.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- NIS2 / ISO 27001 both DEMAND regular exercises, neither says HOW
- Diagnosis: most exercises exist because the auditor asks, so they are built to pass the audit, not to train. Say it once, then leave compliance alone
- [POINT boxes] the four symptoms of an audit-built exercise:
- Don't open up: nobody admits "I don't know" in front of the boss
- Egos clash: IT vs management vs whoever signs, everyone defends their turf
- "Can't happen here": scenario read as fiction, nobody feels the stakes
- Fun taboo: serious topic, so it must be boring, so nobody engages
- Chain: boring → no engagement → no learning → no point
- [FLAT] exercise-haters spend energy faulting the exercise; engaging → they forget to resist
- Duty creates the obligation; the game turns it into competence
:::

## The plan only lives on paper. {.vcenter background-image="images/hero-dead-document.jpg" background-opacity="0.35" background-size="cover"}

::: {.notes}
- Plan from 5 years ago, lives in SharePoint
- Ransomware hits → no SharePoint
- Not anti-plan: the plan is still needed, written down, kept
- Problem is where it lives: only in SharePoint = nobody remembers it at 03:00
- [VERBATIM] "Keep the plan. The exercise is what moves it from SharePoint into people's heads."
:::

## An incident has many seats {.vcenter}

{{< include illus/seat-table.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- [CLICK ×6] Detective · Protector · Tracker · Communicator · Crisis Manager · Threat Hunter
- Tech people overlook soft seats (Communicator, Crisis Manager) = keeping a level head
- Non-technical welcome: method, not specialty
- Hard part: translating for leadership
- [RHETORICAL, self-answer] "How many roles does your plan name? Often fewer than you think. An incident has at least six."
- → straight into "head that isn't yours"
:::

## Think with a head that isn't yours {.vcenter}

::: {.feature-grid style="--fg-cols:2;"}
- A seat you never sit in
- Your colleague's view of the incident
:::

{{< include illus/two-heads.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- Point: play the role you would NOT have in a real incident
- Technician plays Communicator → feels what that seat needs from IT under pressure
- Manager plays Tracker → learns why "just tell me if it's bad" has no answer yet
- Result: teamwork. You understand what the others need, before the real day
- Bonus resilience: the person who always does X is sick → someone has sat there
:::

## Talking is free. Acting costs a roll. {.vcenter}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.feature-grid style="--fg-cols:2;"}
- Doubt? Roll
- Success: cleaner trail
- Failure: muddier trail
- Never the answer
:::

::: {.feature-grid .fragment .fx style="--fg-cols:3; font-size:0.55em; margin-top:0.2em;"}
- Easy: 5+
- Medium: 10+
- Hard: 15+
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
{{< include illus/d20.qmd >}}
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
- [VERBATIM] "Talking is free. Acting costs a dice roll. And what you did beforehand loads the die."
- Free ≠ irrelevant: talking is what you're scored on; die = how clean the trail
- Doubt-first: no doubt → succeeds, no roll
- [CLICK bands] Easy 5+ · Medium 10+ · Hard 15+; good question → IM drops a band
- Success example: cert error + encrypted traffic to unknown IP. Cleaner, still incomplete
- NEVER CUT
- [EXIT, VERBATIM] "That is the whole machinery. Talking, one roll, a price. Now the scenario is yours."
:::

```{=html}
<div class="poll-frame live-frame" data-live-src="https://app.wooclap.com/events/SRCIDYA/questions/6aa1086aa3e3f5575beff39f" data-live-title="Live vote result"></div>
```

::: {.notes}
- Chart live. Code showing → alt-tab Wooclap
- React to split, ONE sentence, then prices (scenario facts):
- A cable: encryption stops, disk + logs kept; lose live picture, R2 can't say if they're still inside
- B isolate: spread contained, not source; R2 no entry point, citizen services told at 09:00 anyway
- C leadership: decision has a signature; R2 09:25, mayor has opinion, drive encrypting 45 min
- [LANDING] "All three are defensible. None is free."
- Trap: nobody chose "wait": also a choice, price = drive still encrypting
- [VERBATIM] "You don't get to avoid the loss. You get to pick which one you can defend at 09:00."
- 30 seconds, half the facts, an opinion; at a table you defend it out loud
- [CALLBACK] scored on the reasoning, not the letter
- [BRIDGE] one more thing on a real table before anyone acts
:::

## THE PRESUMPTION DECK {.vcenter}

::: {.presumption-cards}
![](images/type-ransomware.png){.fragment .fx}
![](images/confidence-confident.png){.fragment .fx}
:::

::: {.notes}
- [VERBATIM] "You just picked a letter in thirty seconds. At a real table you also put a card down, face down: what you think this is and how sure you are. That is the part a poll cannot do."
- Round 1 ends: card FACE DOWN, what is it + how sure
- Flip SIMULTANEOUSLY
- Agree + confident → play on. Split, or confident + wrong → STOP: what did you SEE, what did you ASSUME
- [SAY] confidence card = the number your questionnaire tries to measure, here against what happened
- Next slide. Don't talk over the flip
:::

## {.vcenter}

::: {.card style="text-align:center; max-width:700px; margin:0 auto;"}
[Confident. Wrong. Followed.]{style="font-family:'Bebas Neue',sans-serif; font-size:1.5em;"}
:::

{{< include illus/gauge.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- [SILENCE 3s] after the line
- [SLOW, VERBATIM] "The worst thing that can happen is being totally confident about something that's wrong, and everyone else following along, because you seem sure."
- Seattle [~15s]: kids hunted WHO clicked instead of solving
- [BRIDGE] not "be less certain" → make "I'm not sure" safe to say out loud, before reality forces it
:::

## A wrong theory costs time. {.vcenter}

{{< include illus/hourglass.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- [VERBATIM] "A wrong theory doesn't lose the game. It costs time."
- Consequence: table played Ransomware, Confident. It was credential theft. R2: 20 min restoring backups, attacker still had domain admin
- [VERBATIM] "Remember 03:20. Confident, ransomware. It was stolen credentials. They restored backups while the attacker kept domain admin. That is how the drive was encrypting at 08:40 when you voted. The wrong theory at night is the price you paid this morning."
- Table's conclusion IS the R2 working theory, like reality
- [BRIDGE] "Confidence against outcome. That is one of four things an exercise measures."
:::

## What an exercise measures. {.vcenter}

::: {.feature-grid style="--fg-cols:2;"}
- Time to escalate
- Who got called
- Decisions on half the facts
- Confidence vs outcome
:::

{{< include illus/form.qmd >}}

::: {.notes}
- [VERBATIM] "This is what an exercise measures. A questionnaire can't."
- Replacement evidence: hand leadership THIS, not the questionnaire
- Observed, not stated: a clock, a phone log, a card
- Last one = the presumption card, just seen
- Debrief 5-20 min writes them down = the artifact
- Starter guide: free, malwareandmonsters.com; full CTA at the end
:::
